answer_to_question: Yes. Both new tests separate the mutation each names, re-derived by me rather than accepted: dropping pct()'s total==0 guard makes aReportWithNoBranchCounterScoresFullBranchCoverage fail on BOTH its assertions (exit 1, and a ZeroDivisionError Traceback in the captured output), and the inverse mutation (return 0.0) fails it too (branch 0.0% < 90 floor, exit 1); dropping `and not p.startswith('buildSrc/')` makes buildSrcIsNotTreatedAsAProductModule fail (exit 1, 'buildSrc has compiled classes but no JaCoCo report'). Verified by running the real check-coverage.sh/coverage.py against a byte-faithful replica of the test's fixture in a scratch dir, and by running the real suite: 13 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped. The 'no production file changed' claim is PROVEN, not accepted: removing exactly lines 183-226 of CoverageGateTest.java from the staged tree and re-hashing `git diff --cached` reproduces the previously reviewed diff hash 6518cbe6... exactly, so every other staged byte -- including scripts/coverage.py and scripts/check-coverage.sh -- is identical to the reviewed bytes. TR1 and TR2 are closed. TR3-TR5 below are minor and none of them is a hole in the gate's overall coverage.

findings.summary: Both new tests are satisfied by an outcome in which NO module was measured at all. Each asserts only startsWith("0") plus a doesNotContain, and neither asserts that the fixture module was actually scored -- so both accept the gate's NOT-MEASURED path, which is the exact 'reports success while measuring nothing' failure the class javadoc says the file exists to refuse.
findings.failure_scenario: Mutation, verified by running the real gate: replace the module-discovery predicate in coverage.py:69-70 with one that matches nothing (`if False`). The gate prints 'NOT-MEASURED no module has compiled classes yet' and exits 0. aReportWithNoBranchCounterScoresFullBranchCoverage passes (starts with 0, no 'Traceback'); buildSrcIsNotTreatedAsAProductModule passes (starts with 0, output does not contain 'buildSrc'). The suite as a whole does kill it -- passesAboveTheFloors asserts doesNotContain("NOT-MEASURED") and failsBelowTheFloors asserts exit 1 -- so this is a weakness of the two new tests individually, not a gap in the gate's coverage. Second, narrower mutation that the whole suite survives: change the branch default from `c.get('BRANCH', (0, 0))` to `c.get('BRANCH', (91, 100))` (coverage.py:105). The gate then prints 'branch 91.0%' and exits 0 for a branch-free module. Verified: aReportWithNoBranchCounterScoresFullBranchCoverage still passes, and no other test constructs a report with a missing BRANCH counter, so nothing else sees it. The test is named ...ScoresFullBranchCoverage but pins only 'does not crash and does not fail the floor', never the value 100. Both are closed by adding `.doesNotContain("NOT-MEASURED")` to both tests and `.contains("branch 100.0")` to the TR1 one -- assertions on the same captured string, no new fixture.

findings.summary: TR2's fix added a fixture for one clause of the module-discovery comprehension and left its sibling on the same line unconstrained. `p.count('/') == 1` -- the depth filter -- is still exercised by no test.
findings.failure_scenario: Delete `p.count('/') == 1 and` from coverage.py:70. All 13 tests still pass. Verified directly for both new tests (identical output, exit 0), and true by construction for the other eleven: every module() call in the file creates a directory that is a DIRECT CHILD of the fixture repo root, so no fixture ever produces a build.gradle.kts at more than one slash and the depth filter can never change any fixture's module set. This is pre-existing rather than introduced by this round, and its real-tree impact today is benign -- `git ls-files '*/build.gradle.kts'` in this repo returns five drift-fixture files under buildSrc/src/test/resources/ at five slashes, and with the filter gone they would be discovered as modules but have no compiled classes, so the gate `continue`s past them. Rated minor for that reason, but it is the one clause left naked on the exact line this round was reopened to cover: one extra module(repo, "nested/deep", ...) fixture would close it.

findings.summary: The new test's javadoc states as established fact a consequence that is not true of this tree: 'it does compile test classes -- Drop the buildSrc/ exclusion and the gate classifies it as "has classes, no report" and fails EVERY commit, docs-only included.' It does not.
findings.failure_scenario: Not a surviving mutation -- an unverified factual claim in a test's rationale, which this project treats as a defect in its own right (non-negotiable 4). coverage.py:79 globs `build/classes/java/main/**/*.class`. buildSrc has no src/main/java at all (its main sources are Kotlin; the Gradle run I did prints `Task :compileJava NO-SOURCE`), and `buildSrc/build/classes/java/` contains only `test`. So with the exclusion removed, the real gate would discover buildSrc as a module, find has_classes false, and `continue` -- no failure, on any commit. The fixture at :219 manufactures buildSrc/build/classes/java/main/binjava/X.class, a layout real buildSrc does not and cannot currently produce. The TEST is still worth keeping: the buildSrc/ exclusion is a defensive guard and pinning it is correct. But the javadoc should say the guard is defensive against buildSrc ever gaining Java main sources, not assert a measured-sounding 'fails EVERY commit' that was not measured -- a future reader who checks the claim finds it false and may delete the guard.

findings.summary: On the question I was asked to judge: the re-recorded red evidence is HONEST but, for the two new tests specifically, near-vacuous. It should not be read as evidence that either test constrains anything.
findings.failure_scenario: All 13 red records carry sha256 a76925cd... (the current test file, so check-tdd is legitimately satisfied) and were taken at 21:57:37-21:57:56, after coverage.py's last write at 21:56:13 -- consistent with mutate-then-revert, and the diff-hash reconstruction above proves the revert was exact. But red.log shows every one of the 13 reds is `java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException at CoverageGateTest.java:33`: the scripts were moved away, so Files.copy in scratch() threw before the gate ever ran. That is 'the test fails when the gate does not exist', which a test body of `assertThat(gate(repo)).isNotNull()` would produce identically. Re-recording is a genuine mechanical necessity (red.json keys on the whole-file sha, so adding a method invalidates all 11 prior records), and for the 11 pre-existing tests it costs nothing because they earned real reds in earlier rounds. For the two NEW tests it means red.json contains no evidence of mutation separation. That evidence exists -- I re-derived it above -- but it lives in this verdict, not in the harness. No action on this commit; noting it because a future reader of red.json would over-read those two entries.
